Definition: from G243 and G1085; foreign, i.e. not a Jew:--stranger.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in the story of the ten lepers: There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger. The word is the foreigner, the one not a Jew, and the only one of the ten who came back to thank Jesus was a Samaritan, a stranger to the promises.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a stranger carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the sting in it, that the foreigner thanked God while the nine who belonged went home silent.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
